plans.summary:
Cause and owner: index.html groups Skills and Sites inside Controls, and both feature renderers refresh when that dropdown opens. The governing principle is predictable capability entry points using one shared interaction style. Strengthen the existing navigation components in common.js and base.css; retain Skills and Knowledge Hub as the owners of their actions and data.

Task #1 - Split the navigation. In index.html, place right-aligned dropdowns in the order Skills, Sites, Settings, followed by the existing New Goal group. Rename Controls and its accessible label to Settings. Move the existing Skill and site list containers into their respective dropdowns, retaining the other Settings controls and their destinations.

Task #2 - Connect the existing actions. In settings_skills.js, show applicable enabled Custom Skills, then a separator followed by New Skill and Manage Skills. Use openSkillEditor() and #/settings/skills. In knowledge-hub.js, show sites, then a separator followed by New Site and Manage Sites. Use editHubSite() and #/settings/knowledge-hub. Preserve Skill parameter collection, agent tabs, command-palette discovery, and published/draft site opening in new tabs.

Task #3 - Complete shared menu behavior. Rebind each list's opening refresh to its new dropdown. Preserve refresh after edits and context changes, rejecting stale responses in both success and failure paths. Keep creation and management entries visible when lists are empty or unavailable, with unavailable actions handled consistently for detached contexts. Extend the shared dismissal handler as needed so all menus close on action selection, outside click, Escape, or opening another menu; keyboard focus should remain usable.

Task #4 - Apply existing visual conventions. Reuse shared summary, panel, icon, management-row, spacing, and theme styles. Add one reusable separator style using existing tokens. Adjust the responsive topbar only as needed so the added buttons and open panels remain reachable without clipping on narrow screens.

Task #5 - Align navigation guidance. Update affected Guide, onboarding, Skill-editor, and Todo text. Update the corresponding checkout intent documents for navigation, Skills, Knowledge Hub, Events, and Toolbar references to describe the new entry points while retaining existing management routes.

Task #6 - Verify the resulting behavior. Update static_surface/navigation.rs and affected browser expectations; add focused topbar coverage for exact order, exclusive menu contents, separators, all four creation/management actions, Skill launch, and published/draft site links. Exercise empty/error states, context switching with delayed responses, keyboard dismissal, light/dark themes, and narrow layouts. Run focused browser tests with Chromium available and confirm they actually execute, then static asset checks and the configured workflow checks on the replacement candidate. Compare any suspected baseline failure against pinned commit 139e2dd39781896779b18ae7ecb004f068c71daa before classifying it; preserve earlier work and reports as history.

skill.prompt:
## Implementation

Implement the current Goal Round using all accepted plans and attached Skills. Inspect existing code, make the complete change, run appropriate verification, and report evidence for each checklist item. Check the plan's assumptions against the code and keep policy in its shared owner. Prefer one correction that explains the affected behavior over separate fixes at each failing call site. Report evidence-backed plan deviations within the Goal's scope and existing authority. Preserve unrelated changes and historical evidence.

### Intent and architecture

Review Refine's relevant documentation files under Refine's runtime at `<refine-runtime>/docs/intent/***/*.*` as the durable product specification.

### Semantic code organization

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

If issues outside the Goal’s scope block progress, investigate and fix them or use an evidence-backed workaround, preserving required checks and documenting what you changed.
